findings.highlight: I was having a perfectly good time up until now…
findings.evidenceJa: 引っ越し前のクソ忙しいときに、いきなり空気読まない招かれざる客が来るまではな！
findings.explanation: Haruki says he was in a fine mood until socially oblivious uninvited guests suddenly arrived during the insanely busy period before the move. Todokanai TL cuts the whole accusation after 'until,' omits the punchline that answers their complaint about his mood, and leaves the quotation unfinished.
findings.japanese:
「さっきまでは悪くなかったよ。
……引っ越し前のクソ忙しいときに、
いきなり空気読まない招かれざる客が来るまではな！」
findings.todokanai: "I was having a perfectly good time up until now…

findings.evidenceJa: どうせお前らも昨日はベッタベタしてたんだろ？
findings.explanation: Takeya adds that Haruki and Setsuna were surely glued all over each other yesterday too. Todokanai TL omits the tease and leaves the quotation open; more importantly, it deletes the 'too' that Haruki later identifies as Takeya's revealing narrative trick.
findings.japanese:
「いや、来るなら今日しかないかなって。
明日は引越し前日だし、昨夜はイブだし。
……どうせお前らも昨日はベッタベタしてたんだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "I felt today would be our only chance to drop by, ya know? Tomorrow will be the day before moving day, and yesterday was Christmas Eve…

findings.highlight: "Hmmm? What about you back then? What are you saying you felt about me back then?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「ん～？　あの頃のあんたはどうだったって？
……あの頃のあたしは、どうだったって～？」
findings.explanation: Io presses what Takeya was like then and what she herself was like then; 'what you felt about me' turns the second prompt into a direct romantic confession — The almost-confession and embarrassed stop remain.
findings.japanese:
「ん～？　あの頃のあんたはどうだったって？
……あの頃のあたしは、どうだったって～？」
findings.todokanai: "Hmmm? What about you back then? What are you saying you felt about me back then?"

findings.highlight: The smile on her face no longer bears the sense of sadness and loneliness that I saw back then,
findings.evidenceJa: 無理めに感情を盛り上げた、テンションの高い笑顔でもない。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's smile is neither the sad lonely smile of that period nor the artificially high-energy smile she used to force her emotions upward. Todokanai TL omits the second false smile, leaves the sentence on a comma, and weakens the contrast that establishes her present laughter as genuine.
findings.japanese:
あの頃の、悲しげで寂しげな笑顔じゃない。
無理めに感情を盛り上げた、
テンションの高い笑顔でもない。
findings.todokanai: The smile on her face no longer bears the sense of sadness and loneliness that I saw back then,

findings.highlight: Did he have any lame hero's journey stories?
findings.evidenceJa: なんか嫌な武勇伝とかないかな？
findings.explanation: 武勇伝 means boast-worthy exploits or legendary anecdotes; Setsuna asks for some awful, embarrassing 'legend' from Haruki's unpleasant past. 'Hero's journey stories' is a different literary concept and produces unnatural dialogue that does not describe the requested dirt.
findings.japanese:
「ねぇねぇ、あの頃の春希くんの話、もっと聞かせてよ。
すっごく性格悪かったはずだよね？
なんか嫌な武勇伝とかないかな？」
findings.todokanai: "Come on, lemme hear all about Haruki-kun back then. His personality must've been awful. Did he have any lame hero's journey stories?"

findings.highlight: I bet you got a promotion to a supervisory role
findings.evidenceJa: お局になって実権を手に入れただけじゃないの？
findings.explanation: Tomo jokes that Io has become the office battle-axe or entrenched senior woman and merely acquired de facto power. Todokanai TL converts the gendered workplace insult and informal clout into a literal promotion, flattening why Io immediately rejects the label rather than discussing a new job title.
findings.japanese: 「お局になって実権を手に入れただけじゃないの？」
findings.todokanai: "I bet you got a promotion to a supervisory role, and now you enjoy toying with those under you."

findings.highlight: all the escapades of your youth…
findings.evidenceJa: そこまで青臭い話を俺に喋っちまったこと。
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether Takeya will regret telling him such painfully earnest, idealistic talk about marriage, children, and parental leave. Todokanai TL calls it 'escapades of your youth,' relocating the content into past adventures that Takeya never narrated.
findings.japanese:
「いや、そこまで青臭い話を俺に喋っちまったこと。
……俺なら明日頭抱えてるレベル」
findings.todokanai: "No, I meant how you just told me about all the escapades of your youth… If I were you, I'd be burying my head in embarrassment."

findings.highlight: Time will inevitably cause our own affairs and the affairs of others around us to converge.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの事情も、その近くで起こっていた事情も、いつか時間と共に収束していく。
findings.explanation: With time, each situation—the couple's and the nearby couple's—will settle or reach its own resolution. Todokanai TL says the affairs converge with one another, replacing the theme of individual conflicts resolving over time with a claim that their stories merge.
findings.japanese:
俺たちの事情も、
その近くで起こっていた事情も、
いつか時間と共に収束していく。
findings.todokanai: Time will inevitably cause our own affairs and the affairs of others around us to converge.
